reason: The bone-lineage environment should direct stem-cell descendants toward the cells needed for living bone.
expectation: The cells will develop toward a bone-forming lineage.

effect: The lineage produces osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes, giving me cells to incorporate into the bone construction.
reaction: The distinction between matrix-producing osteoblasts and embedded osteocytes is useful.
reason: Mineral should reinforce the collagen framework of the arm bones.
expectation: The mineral will combine with the collagen framework to form a stronger bone structure.

effect: The framework is mineralised but still needs living cells and a blood supply.
reaction: The contrast between collagen's toughness and mineral's compression resistance is useful.
reason: Bone cells should make the mineralised framework part of a living bone construction.
expectation: The bone cells will be incorporated into the mineralised arm bones.

effect: The cells must be linked to a blood supply before joining the bone framework; the picture also shows nutrients reaching osteocytes through small channels.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the required order after my incorrect guess.
reason: The supplied bone cells should now be ready to join the mineralised framework.

choice.combine: Bone cells linked to a blood supply

expectation: The supplied cells will be incorporated into the arm bone framework.

effect: The supplied cells and mineralised framework formed living arm bones, completing the bone goal and revealing the joint goal.
reaction: The nutrient-channel detail reinforces how embedded bone cells are supplied.
reason: The synovial membrane should line the inner face of the fibrous joint sleeve.
expectation: They will form a lined joint capsule.

effect: The sleeve and membrane formed a synovial capsule, completing the lined-capsule goal.
reaction: The distinction between the fibrous sleeve and its fluid-producing lining is clear.
reason: Articular cartilage should cover the ends of the living bones where they meet.
expectation: The arm bones will acquire smooth cartilage-covered joint surfaces.

effect: The arm bones now have cartilage-covered surfaces that can slide against one another.
reaction: The sliding-surface inset makes the cartilage's role clear.
reason: The synovial capsule should surround the cartilage-covered bone ends to form the joint.
expectation: The capsule will join the bones around the elbow joint.

effect: The capsule now encloses the cartilage-covered bone ends, with fluid in the joint space; the elbow still needs support.
reaction: The connection between the lining's fluid and gliding surfaces is clear.
reason: The elbow ligaments should support the enclosed joint by spanning its sides.
expectation: The ligaments will reinforce the elbow while allowing movement.

effect: The ligaments completed the movable arm skeleton, with the planned picture showing elbow bending and resistance to sideways movement; all goals are complete.
reaction: The final cutaway brings the supporting and moving parts together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Building the joint from cartilage, capsule and ligaments was worthwhile because the planned pictures connect each structure to gliding or restraint.

leastWorthwhile.text: The bone-cell supply picture was useful but appeared again in the completed bone cutaway, making that passage somewhat repetitive.

surprise.text: I expected bone cells to join the mineralised framework directly; instead, they first combined with blood vessels. The picture showed nutrients reaching embedded cells through tiny channels.

arbitrary.text: Requiring the blood supply to be linked to the cells before adding them to the framework felt like a game-specific ordering constraint, although the supply itself had a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: assembling the joint made the relationship between its structures and movement interesting, and I would be curious to see how muscle adds to it.
